paper.title_en: Applications of quantum remote sensing in aerospace information systems
paper.abstract_en: Quantum remote sensing is defined as a theoretical and methodological framework that characterizes the laws of motion of remote sensing phenomena at the quantum level. It is grounded in quantum mechanics, employs the Schrödinger equation and quantum states as its principal modes of representation, and takes as its object of study the dynamic, multispatiotemporal planetary–Earth system. The field encompasses a comprehensive technological system, including theory, information processing, experimentation, computation, imaging, spectroscopy, measurement, and application. Its central objective is to investigate how information can be expressed, transmitted, and ultimately perceived through quantum states across the entire sensing chain. Compared with classical approaches, quantum remote sensing enables the acquisition of weaker, more microscopic, deeper, and richer information. Quantum remote sensing was first proposed internationally by Professor Bi Siwen in 2000. The research program identifies four principal challenges: how to characterize the laws of motion of remote sensing processes at the quantum scale; how to realize the expression, transmission, and perceptual reception of information via quantum states; how quantum spectral imaging can be achieved, with emphasis on the characteristics of quantum spectra and the governing laws of spectral imaging; and how to conduct experimental investigations of quantum light-field imaging, as well as to advance the practical implementation and industrialization of quantum remote sensing imaging technologies. Over twenty-six years of investigation, this research has yielded more than ten original innovations and has led to the development of eight prototype systems for quantum detection and quantum imaging. The work also presents an overview of the research team, its scientific outputs, and associated recognitions and awards. At the systems level, an integrated panoramic framework for aerospace information-based quantum remote sensing is proposed. This framework comprises three principal components: quantum detection and sensing systems for aerospace information (0.5–900m range); quantum lidar systems (1–50km range); and quantum remote sensing observation systems (80, 300, and 500–800km orbital regimes). The implementation of a quantum remote sensing scientific experimental satellite is further proposed, including the planned development, launch, and operation of a globally pioneering quantum remote sensing satellite. From a technological perspective, such systems offer substantial advantages, with significant implications for both aerospace information applications and military utilization. The research team has completed studies on spaceborne active quantum remote sensing imaging schemes. The application of quantum remote sensing satellites is expected to have profound and far-reaching significance, particularly in the context of the emerging aerospace information.
